title: DARKEST
REFINED
renders.tagline: Familiar heroes. New possibilities.

renders.title: HEALING, SHARED
renders.lead: A party that holds without a Vestal or a Jester.
items: Arbalest · Battlefield Bandage
Cures bleed and heals 3–7, a healer for bleed dungeons.
Plague Doctor · Battlefield Medicine
Cures blight and heals 3–7, a healer for blight dungeons.
Flagellant · Suffer
Takes on an ally's bleed and blight and relieves 4–6 stress.
Man-at-Arms · Bolster
Relieves 1–3 stress for the whole party, no per-battle limit.

renders.title: MANY HANDS ON THE MARK
renders.lead: Marking no longer depends on the Arbalest and the Bounty Hunter.
items: Grave Robber · Thrown Dagger
Damage vs. marked raised from +25–40% to +40–80%.
Musketeer · Mark the Quarry
Marks the target and cuts PROT by 20–30% (3 turns).
REWORKED
Bounty Hunter · Mark for Death
Damage taken +15–25%, so the whole party benefits.
Arbalest · Sniper Shot
+60–100% damage vs. marked, ignores guard.

renders.title: PULL THE BACK LINE IN
renders.lead: Skills that pull enemies grew from four in the original to eight.
items: Plague Doctor · Disorienting Blast
Instead of a random shuffle, stuns an enemy in ranks 2–4 and pulls it 2.
Bounty Hunter · Come Hither
Pulls an enemy in ranks 3–4 forward 3, SPD −4 to −8 (3 turns), to finish in rank 1.
Arbalest · Bola
Instead of knocking back ranks 1–2, pulls one enemy in ranks 2–4 forward 2.
Duelist · Disengage
Steps back and pulls one enemy in ranks 2–4 forward 2 for the front line.

renders.title: REFINED, NOT REINVENTED
renders.lead: Every change is tuned inside the original game's own rules, so it never feels foreign.
items: The same tension
Every buff carries a price. The game stays as hard as you remember.
Clear guardrails
Class trinkets and each hero's official lore set the limits of every change.
Measured, then tuned
Game data, a comparison model and real play decide the numbers.
Built with players
Every comment is read, and every change keeps a written reason.

title: DARKEST
REFINED
renders.tagline: Familiar heroes. New possibilities.
Mark, hook, execute.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Flashbang was simply better than Uppercut, every marking skill was nearly the same, and his finishing tools rarely lined up.
THE DIRECTION
One clear routine for a professional: mark the target, hook it forward, finish it.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Mark for Death makes the target take +15–25% damage; Come Hither pulls 3 ranks and slows; Finish Him hits stunned and bleeding foes harder, but only from ranks 1–2.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Caltrops from any rank bleeds both back ranks, then Uppercut stuns and Finish Him closes it out from the front.

renders.tagline: Restraint becomes the beast's power.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Transforming dumped stress on every ally, so the beast often stayed in its chains.
THE DIRECTION
Human form gives up a little accuracy for a harder-hitting Beast's Bile; the beast's price moves onto himself, so transforming is a real choice.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
He carries the cost himself: self stress +12, allies only +5. Transforming heals 8–12 and the beast gains CRIT +6–10%.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Keep your stress in check with Absolution, then spend it to unleash the beast.

renders.tagline: She makes the others stronger.
rows: THE PROBLEM
She paid the bills and sat out the real fights, so she was left behind before the Darkest Dungeon.
THE DIRECTION
Weak until Veteran, strong from Champion, and her strength goes into the rest of the party.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Fortifying Vapours makes healing received +20% (+40% at level 5, stacking); at level 5 Protect Me lends her guard a riposte, Nervous Stab marks and Get Down! clears her mark.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Bring her for the party: boost the healer and arm the bodyguard. Her Flashpowder lowers dodge and move resist so hits and pulls land; its burn is 1–2, then 7 at level 5.

renders.tagline: The crossbow that rallies the party.
rows: THE PROBLEM
She simply offered less than the Vestal or Occultist: weaker heals, no better utility or damage. She shone only in mark parties, and mark parties were niche.
THE DIRECTION
Widen her healing, let her relieve stress too, and raise her attacks so she pressures enemy ranks 3–4 harder than before.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Battlefield Bandage cures bleed; Rallying Flare relieves 2–4 stress for the whole party, herself included, and no longer clears mark and stun.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Bola pulls a rank 2–4 enemy 2 ranks toward your front line; Suppressing Fire slows the back two and lowers their ACC; Sniper Shot fires past Guard.

renders.tagline: The holy knight can carry the party's healing.
rows: THE PROBLEM
His signature stun was unreliable, Zealous Accusation had no reason to be picked, and his healing lagged behind dedicated healers.
THE DIRECTION
A slow, steadfast knight: make each signature tool dependable and let him be a primary healer.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Stunning Blow gets a strong stun (110% chance); Battle Heal restores 3–4 (6–7 at level 5) and raises PROT; Inspiring Cry grows every level. Bulwark of Faith no longer raises the torch.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
From any rank, Bulwark of Faith steels him against stuns and death blows for the rest of the battle.

renders.tagline: Back to the base game's rules.
rows: THE PROBLEM
His bleed resist and speed growth sat above the base game's usual caps, and his stun and move resists above the baseline, with no reason in his lore.
THE DIRECTION
Follow the base game's own rules, and make his self-sacrifice useful from level 1.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Stun and move resist back to 40, bleed to 60, speed growth 6/6/7/7/8. Endure no longer speeds him up.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Endure relieves 12–16 stress (a net 8 after its own cost); Suffer takes an ally's bleed and blight and eases their stress by 4–6.

renders.tagline: More than one dagger worth throwing.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Thrown Dagger's built-in accuracy buff made it the skill you always picked, and Toxin Trickery was almost never taken.
THE DIRECTION
Spread her value across the kit so more skills earn a slot, and let her join mark parties.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
The accuracy buff moves to Poison Darts; Thrown Dagger hits marked targets harder (+40–80%); Toxin Trickery heals 1–5 with smaller, shorter buffs.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
A self-sustaining skirmisher who fits mark parties without leaning on one skill.

renders.tagline: She never tires. Now neither does her kit.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Her strongest skills left her exhausted for the whole battle, at odds with a warrior whose lore says she never tires, and her kit collapsed into one fixed set.
THE DIRECTION
Remove exhaustion and keep her relentless, paying for it elsewhere in her kit.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Breakthrough, Bleed Out and Barbaric YAWP! no longer exhaust her. YAWP trades its stun for her attack buff; Breakthrough hits a little softer.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
YAWP has no use limit and cows every enemy into hitting softer; Adrenaline Rush heals 3–7 and Wicked Hack is now a real pick.

renders.tagline: Ranged and melee builds both work.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Riposte came only from Duelist's Advance, which steps him forward and breaks a ranged formation, and Point Blank Shot hit hard for only a one-rank recoil.
THE DIRECTION
Let both the gunslinger and the duelist stand on their own.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Tracking Shot grants riposte without moving; Duelist's Advance gives a stacking combat buff; Point Blank Shot recoils him 2 ranks and knocks the target back 3.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Hold the back with pistol and riposte, or step in as a duelist with Wicked Slice and Open Vein.

renders.tagline: Less damage, more protection.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Hound's Rush out-damaged the true mark dealers while his protective tools were too weak to bother with.
THE DIRECTION
A protector who spreads bleed from range and leaves the big marked hits to others.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Hound's Rush works from any rank but hits softer (DMG −40%); Blackjack drops to a normal stun; his extra blight and bleed resist are gone.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Guard Dog gives +20–30% dodge, Cry Havoc heals 4–6 party stress more reliably, and Lick Wounds works from any rank.

renders.tagline: Still the best stress healer.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Solo rarely earned a slot, and Battle Ballad duplicated the Man-at-Arms' Command.
THE DIRECTION
Keep him the best stress healer while other heroes gain alternatives.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Battle Ballad trades its accuracy for more crit (+4–8%); Solo works from any rank with more dodge and a bigger Finale.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
A spotlight Jester: Solo scrambles the enemy formation, clears corpses, and lifts his allies' marks while marking himself.

renders.tagline: A fallen king who leads the charge.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Intimidate was a support debuff that clashed with a king carried by his followers, and Revenge cost too much early on.
THE DIRECTION
His lore sets the role: a front-line blow that leads the fight.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Intimidate becomes Sunder: a rank-1 strike that cracks PROT by 30–50% for 3 turns (130% chance). It no longer reaches every rank. Revenge's cost now grows with level.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Open armored foes for the whole party before the heavy swings land. Chop, Hew and Purge each gain 5 accuracy.

renders.tagline: The veteran who holds the line.
rows: THE PROBLEM
His damage sat below what his kit predicts, Command copied the Jester's Ballad, and party stress relief rested on the Jester.
THE DIRECTION
A veteran bodyguard who steadies and leads his allies.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Bolster becomes a repeatable party stress heal (1–3); Command gives PROT +10–15% and removes stun, but no crit.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Rampart stuns from ranks 1–2 without shuffling him forward, and Retribution cracks armor for the next blows.

renders.tagline: Curses that set up the whole party.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Vulnerability Hex was just another mark, and many players stopped Wyrd Reconstruction at level 4.
THE DIRECTION
A debuffer whose curses enable the party's stuns, bleeds and physical hits.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Weakening Curse cuts PROT by 25–35%; Vulnerability Hex lowers five resistances by 20–25%; Daemon's Pull drags rank 4 to the front. The hex no longer lowers dodge.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Hex a target, then stun, bleed or crack it. Hands from the Abyss now stuns a rank 1–2 enemy from ranks 3–4, at ACC 80. Level-5 Wyrd Reconstruction keeps the level-4 bleed risk.

renders.tagline: Each healer gets her own niche.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Battlefield Medicine cured everything for everyone, Incision was rarely worth a slot, and Disorienting Blast overlapped the Bounty Hunter's Flashbang.
THE DIRECTION
Give each healer a clear niche: blight for her, bleed for the Arbalest.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Battlefield Medicine heals 3 (7 at level 5) and cures an ally's blight only; no free self-cleanse. Incision gains accuracy. Disorienting Blast pulls 2 ranks instead of shuffling.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Bring her to blight-heavy dungeons with the Arbalest; Disorienting Blast stuns an enemy in ranks 2–4 and drags it toward your front line.

renders.tagline: The DLC outlier, back in line.
rows: THE PROBLEM
Pierce did everything on one cheap skill, her speed grew faster than any base-game hero's, and her stun and move resists sat above the baseline.
THE DIRECTION
The dancer who shakes up the enemy line, and the only hero with two skills that pull enemies forward.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Pierce loses rank 4; weapon and speed growth follow the standard curve; stun and move resist 30. Puncture pulls 1 rank instead of 2, and Expose drops its slow and crit debuff.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Expose reveals a hidden back-liner and drags it 2 ranks forward; Puncture breaks guard and PROT. Serpent Sway brings her back to rank 1, and Impale blights from level 1.

renders.tagline: A front-rank Vestal is now an option.
rows: THE PROBLEM
The rear Vestal's fixed rotation left no room for other builds.
THE DIRECTION
Let her fight from the front without losing her rear-rank strengths.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Mace Bash heals her 3–5; Divine Grace works from any rank; Judgement loses its self-heal.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Bash and heal from rank 2, or stay back with Divine Comfort; Illumination strips dodge 15–25% and burns 1–3 from any rank.

renders.tagline: No longer an Arbalest copy.
rows: THE PROBLEM
The Musketeer was an exact copy of the Arbalest, with nothing of her own.
THE DIRECTION
Rebuild her from her lore: a celebrated sharpshooter hunting monsters to become a legend.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Piercing Ball reaches every rank and pierces 25–50% armor; Smokescreen stuns the front two; Covering Smoke hides an ally. Less HP and speed than the Arbalest.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
A back-rank hunter who shields allies with smoke; Patch Up now also eases 2–4 stress.

renders.tagline: The riposte stays. The overkill goes.
rows: THE PROBLEM

One of the strongest heroes in the base game: Coup de Grâce reached every rank from any position, ignored protection and gave an extra action on a kill, and The Boot stunned and pushed for little cost.
THE DIRECTION
Keep the riposte duelist whole, and trim her direct offense so the counterattack plan stays her main strength.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Coup de Grâce DMG −70% (was −60%); The Boot DMG −60% (was −40%), its heavy kick now pushing 2 ranks; Flèche +20% (was +25%). Feint's riposte boost is 10–30% and Touché's dodge 30–40%.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Disengage now pulls a rank 2–4 enemy 2 ranks forward as she leaps back, drawing it into your front line's reach.

renders.tagline: Advance from the rear. Temper the fire.
rows: THE PROBLEM
From the back rank she could keep Burn stacking through long fights, and her kit worked from almost anywhere.
THE DIRECTION
Open from ranks 3–4, then step into the fight: keep the strong opening, cut the long-fight burn.
THE SOLUTION, AND ITS PRICE
Ransack and Controlled Burn start from ranks 3–4; Controlled Burn is 3–5 and its ground fire lasts 2 rounds; Backdraft +20% per stack from ranks 1–2; Firefly no longer delays Burn decay.
NEW WAYS TO PLAY
Open with Controlled Burn or Ransack, advance 2 with Hearthlight, then cash in the Burn stacks with Backdraft up front.
